action_plan.title: File a Dubai AI Park entry before August 15.
action_plan.body: Dubai Municipality opened a global AI-driven park-design competition for Al Safa 2 with cash prizes and community voting. This is a free pitch into the exact MENA buyer we want — whoever owns government partnerships should assemble a small AI + urban-design strike team this week.

action_plan.title: Stand up a Seedance 2.5 enterprise pipeline.
action_plan.body: Native 30-second 4K clips with 50 reference inputs ends our segment-stitching workflow for branded video. R&D should request Volcano Engine beta access now so the studio can pitch a single-shot brand spot before competitors get their seats.

action_plan.title: Ship a one-image to 3DGS demo on the studio site.
action_plan.body: TripoSplat is MIT-licensed and runs with near-zero dependencies — a junior dev can put a working image-to-splat experience on the homepage. Whoever runs the web team should make this the next showcase tile to convert GCC inbound.

action_plan.title: Open a channel to the Gulf's new AI infra layer.
action_plan.body: 1001 AI just closed a Lux-led $30M round to wire AI into Gulf heavy industry — they need experience layers on top of their stack. The partnerships function should book an intro call this week before the round noise fades.

coming_next.headline: Seedance 2.5 opens to the public in early July.
coming_next.body: ByteDance is moving the model out of enterprise beta to CapCut, Dreamina, and Doubao consumer surfaces — putting native 30-second 4K in front of 400M+ monthly editors.

coming_next.headline: DeepSeek V4 ships mid-July with peak-valley pricing.
coming_next.body: The official V4 launch will double API rates during peak hours — a quiet pivot from flat pricing that every downstream agent stack will need to re-cost.

coming_next.headline: AI Engineer World's Fair runs through July 2.
coming_next.body: San Francisco's main agentic-AI floor is live now — every credible MCP, eval, and agent vendor will drop news this week. Worth a remote scrape for shippable patterns.

coming_next.headline: Tesla Optimus V3 starts mass production this quarter.
coming_next.body: Q3 ramp is now public with a stated 10M-unit annual goal — humanoid props enter the realm of possible installation kit for Gulf retail and entertainment activations.

first_of_kind.name: NVIDIA — World-Action Models
first_of_kind.body: NVIDIA published a synthesis arguing the next robotics frontier is models pretrained on video to imagine, then fine-tuned on robot data to act. The same lineage powers installations that respond to the room around them — not just to prompts.

first_of_kind.name: ByteDance Seedance 2.5
first_of_kind.body: First major closed video model to claim native 30-second 4K generation in a single segment, ingesting up to 50 multimodal references — images, audio, 3D white models. The stitching workflow is now legacy.

first_of_kind.name: Krea 2 Raw + Turbo — open weights
first_of_kind.body: Krea released its 12B image model as open weights under a custom enterprise license, generating production-grade stills in roughly two seconds. The Raw/Turbo split is built for live brand systems, not gallery prints.

first_of_kind.name: Latent Spatial Memory for Video World Models
first_of_kind.body: A new paper proposes a persistent spatial memory layer so generative video stops forgetting what's behind the camera between shots. This is the missing piece for long-coherent branded environments and walk-around AR.

partners.name: 1001 AI
partners.body: Just closed $30M led by Lux Capital to wire AI into Gulf heavy industry — a natural anchor for any experiential layer we'd build on top of MENA operational data.

partners.name: Spexi
partners.body: Partnered with Niantic Spatial to turn drone imagery into urban-scale Gaussian splat models — the fastest path to splatting a whole Riyadh or Doha district for a pitch.

partners.name: Splatica
partners.body: Mobile 360-to-3D Gaussian Splatting service, now bundled with Insta360 — a clean prosumer capture front-end if we want to onboard regional creators into our pipeline.

partners.name: VAST-AI-Research
partners.body: Built TripoSplat, the MIT-licensed image-to-3D-Gaussian generator — small enough to drop into any web pipeline without a dependency war.

partners.name: Mother London
partners.body: Made the Claude Super Bowl films that just won the Cannes Film Grand Prix — proof a small, sharp creative shop can out-think the holding companies on AI work.

partners.name: Innovative Dreams
partners.body: The Luma × Wonder Project joint studio for hybrid AI-traditional filmmaking on AWS — the model template if a Gulf studio asks us to set up an in-house AI production line.

patterns.headline: The video workflow just collapsed from stitching to single-shot direction.
patterns.body: Seedance 2.5 generates 30 seconds at native 4K from one prompt with 50 reference inputs. The whole industry of cutting, concatenating, and re-prompting between shots — most of what AI video houses sold last year — becomes overhead, not craft.

patterns.headline: Hardware scarcity is now an XR pricing problem.
patterns.body: Apple raised Vision Pro by $200 to $3,700, plus hikes on Macs, iPads, and HomePod — all blamed on a RAM and storage shortage. Spatial computing's volume play just got pushed further out; the near-term winners will be experiences that run on glasses and browsers, not headsets.

patterns.headline: Commerce is becoming a conversation between agents.
patterns.body: Salesforce shipped Agentforce Commerce GA with Shopper, Buyer, and Merchant agents, days after the Cannes Film Grand Prix went to an ad about resisting ads. The brand's job is no longer to talk to a human directly — it's to be legible, trustworthy, and persuasive to the agent in the middle.

patterns.headline: Gulf governments are buying creative AI competitions, not deliverables.
patterns.body: Dubai Municipality just launched the world's first AI-powered park-design challenge for Al Safa 2 with public voting on shortlisted entries. The pattern repeats from NEOM to Qiddiya — the region is buying processes and showcases, which is exactly the bundle ARlab sells.

signals.headline: ByteDance broke the segment ceiling in AI video.
signals.body: At Volcano Engine FORCE in Beijing, ByteDance unveiled Seedance 2.5 — a model it claims generates 30-second 4K clips natively, no stitching, ingesting up to 50 multimodal references. Enterprise beta is live, public launch targeted for early July; the existing Seedance platform is already at $2B ARR. The MPA cease-and-desist hangover from 2.0 is unresolved.
signals.arlab_use: wire a seedance pipeline into the next brand-film pitch before the western shops catch up.

signals.headline: Meta dropped Ray-Ban from the box and started a price war.
signals.body: Meta and EssilorLuxottica launched Meta Glasses at $299 — at least $80 cheaper than the entry Ray-Ban Meta — under Meta's own brand with new designs. It's a clear signal that the smart-glass category is moving from fashion-partner novelty to platform play, with Display variants seeded above it.
signals.arlab_use: treat sub-$300 glasses as the actual install base our gcc clients are pitching to.

signals.headline: Apple Vision Pro just got $200 more expensive.
signals.body: Apple pushed the M5 Vision Pro to $3,700, alongside hikes on Macs, iPads, MacBook Neo, HomePod, and Apple TV — all blamed on the global RAM and storage crunch. The unit-volume story for headsets just got worse; the browser and smart-glass story just got better.
signals.arlab_use: rebalance the roadmap away from headset-first builds and toward glasses + webgpu.

signals.headline: Cannes' biggest creative prize went to an AI ad mocking AI ads.
signals.body: The Cannes Lions Film Grand Prix went to Anthropic's Claude Super Bowl films by Mother London — two spots arguing there is a time and a place for advertising, released days after OpenAI announced ads inside ChatGPT. Sam Altman publicly accused Anthropic of being deceptive, which only sharpened the campaign.
signals.arlab_use: sell the studio's point of view on ai, not just our ability to make it.

signals.headline: Salesforce shipped commerce agents as a real product.
signals.body: Agentforce Commerce hit GA with three distinct agents — Shopper, Buyer, Merchant — ahead of peak shopping season, and Salesforce now says AI assistants are driving retail traffic up 119%. Brands will spend the next six months making themselves legible to agents, not browsers.
signals.arlab_use: start building the agent-readable layer of every brand site we touch.

signals.headline: Dubai launched the world's first AI-powered park-design challenge.
signals.body: Dubai Municipality opened a global challenge to redesign Al Safa 2 Park using AI across site analysis, climate modelling, and visualisation — with Dh200,000 in cash prizes and community voting on shortlisted entries. Applications close 15 August. This is the GCC's first government-issued open creative AI brief.
signals.arlab_use: file a serious entry — the brief is exactly our bundle.

tools.name: Seedance 2.5 (Volcano Engine beta)
tools.body: Native 30-second 4K AI video with up to 50 reference inputs — the first model that can plausibly deliver a full branded spot from a single prompt without manual stitching.

tools.name: TripoSplat
tools.body: Single-image to 3D Gaussian splat generator, MIT-licensed, ~2,000 lines of code with near-zero dependencies — drop straight into a Three.js or WebGPU stack without a CUDA odyssey.

tools.name: Krea 2 Raw + Turbo (open weights)
tools.body: 12B image model now released as open weights under a custom enterprise licence, generating production stills in roughly two seconds — viable as the image layer for live branded systems.

tools.name: Salesforce Agentforce Commerce
tools.body: GA-stage commerce agents (Shopper, Buyer, Merchant) for brands to expose their catalogue and checkout to conversational AI surfaces — a template for how to make any client agent-ready.

tools.name: Doubao 2.1 Pro (Volcano Engine)
tools.body: ByteDance's production-grade LLM is now serving over 180 trillion tokens a day — a credible non-Western brain for Gulf clients who want distance from the US/EU AI stack.

tools.name: Pika 2.5 with Pikaframes
tools.body: Cinematic short-form video model with frame-anchored extension — useful where Seedance is overkill and we need fast, controllable storyboards for client review.

undisclosed.name: ByteDance's quiet $2B video business
undisclosed.body: While the Seedance 2.5 headlines flew, ByteDance disclosed its enterprise Seedance platform has reached $2B in annual recurring revenue — meaning a Chinese AI video stack is already the size of a public US software company, mostly invisible to Western buyers.

undisclosed.name: Doubao crosses the production threshold
undisclosed.body: Volcano Engine confirmed Doubao 2.1 Pro now serves 180 trillion daily tokens — a 10x surge that puts ByteDance's LLM in the same operational class as OpenAI's deployment. No press tour, just a one-line conference disclosure.

undisclosed.name: Apple's RAM-shortage cover story
undisclosed.body: Apple's $200 Vision Pro hike and price increases across MacBook, iPad, HomePod, and even the new MacBook Neo are all blamed on a RAM and storage shortage. Reads less like an Apple problem and more like a warning shot for every XR/AI vendor with a hardware bill of materials this year.

undisclosed.name: Niantic Spatial × Spexi for physical AI
undisclosed.body: Niantic Spatial quietly partnered with drone-imagery startup Spexi to turn aerial captures into urban-scale Gaussian models for 'physical AI'. The same pipeline that powered Pokémon GO is now mapping cities into splats — the GCC giga-projects are the obvious next customer.
